newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police verge on discovery in mine search.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police verge on discovery in mine search.

text.p: Belgian police, searching a disused coal-mine complex for clues in a sex and murder scandal, found a suspicious bricked-over entrance on Saturday.

Gendarmerie spokesman Guy Soumoy told reporters the 50-strong team found the entrance, filled in with bricks and cement, on the 13th day of searches in the complex and would break through it on Sunday.
"This leads us to believe that there is something else behind," he told reporters. "That can effectively be the hiding place, but we will see tomorrow."

The team, including five architects and geometrists and 12 speleologists, braved the bitter cold in the belief they were on the point of a breakthrough in the search for clues in the child sex and murder scandal which rocked Belgium in August.
Convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux and several alleged accomplices have been detained since August since two young girls were rescued alive from a secret dungeon at a house he owned.
The bodies of four other girls were later found buried at properties connected to Dutroux and an acquaintance, Bernard Weinstein, whose body was also discovered.
The mine search started on December 13 days after Dutroux's second wife Michelle Martin indicated there was something to be found there.
"We have put so much into it because we are certain to find here interesting clues," Soumoy told the reporters.
"The working conditions are difficult for everyone and the cold does not help," he said, saying they were fighting against mud and water and there was a constant danger of a mine gallery collapsing.
The police suspect Dutroux used part of the old tunnels linked through the 24-metre (79-ft deep shaft to hold kidnapped children. He once lived in a caravan near the complex.
Police are now searching for at least seven missing children.
Police said that although the suspicious wall had not been recently bricked over it was difficult to say how long it had been as it was covered in water.
